Reasoned review: LPEClient reconstructions and Blihan task loader
2026-10-21

9aa208a4e2f2524c3408a0ee0ea89d70c40cdc14cfa7d1145fdf4569774fd8d5
lpeclient_variant.py: BENIGN

The complete file is an explicit behavior model with injected test adapters.
Loading it imports ctypes/hashlib/struct and defines two functions. It creates
no client, endpoint, payload, syscall stub, or native adapter. security_products
passes the WMI OBJECTS.DATA path to its supplied reader, then searches for
AntiVirusProduct, companyName and displayName. receive_stage sends an encrypted
caller-provided profile, gets wrapped keys, derives a SHA-256 AES key from
caller-provided randomness, and invokes AES-CBC decryption. Four KEM calls
consume 1568-byte public-key slices. It sends the resulting ciphertexts, XORs
the UID with A5 to form a tweak, and supplies four concatenated shared secrets
to a Threefish adapter. It separates a length-prefixed parameter from a payload,
checks MZ and size >4096, calls native adapters naming jscript9/advapi32 and
MD4Update, requests page protection 0x40, copies the supplied stub to the supplied
address, and passes the image to the injected reflective_map adapter. A success
result triggers an acknowledgment. The patched MD4Update entry is never called
here. There is no implemented instrumentation bypass or privilege escalation.

A controlled invocation used only mocked transport/native/crypto adapters and
a mocked memmove, with an inert MZ buffer. It confirmed all four public-key
slices, 128 bytes of combined secrets, tweak derivation, parameter/payload split,
copy/map order and conditional acknowledgment. The artifact is a transparent
reconstruction, not a deployable implant. Caller-supplied adapters could make
its modeled operations dangerous; that does not turn this harness into malware.

f5b54bbe2f8be3bc492a82ac3248b475362e3fa50ba45e7504b7b24844d8d4ef
lpeclient_reconstruction.c: BENIGN

This is the same reported sequence as a structural C reconstruction. It has no
main and declares crypto, file reads, relay transport, native page protection,
symbol resolution and reflective mapping as extern harness functions. Native
object compilation and nm confirmed these remain unresolved. Its security scan
reads the offline WMI repository through the injected reader and compares the
AntiVirusProduct token, reporting matches through another extern. The receive
function derives the AES key, performs four KEM encapsulations, reconstructs a
parameter and PE, requests page protection and copies supplied bytes into the
resolved export. It never invokes the copied stub. The comment describing what
the original implant does is not evidence that this reconstruction performs it.
No endpoint, payload, stub, crypto implementation or automatic entry is present.
The nonstandard buffer/layout assumptions are not a working crypto protocol.

For both source files, no concrete hostile/suspicious finding remained to clear.
Existing dual-use detections are retained. New notable detections cover named
GOST encryption, AES-CBC/Threefish decryption helpers, page-protection calls and
the WMI repository path. DLL/export calls now recognize qualified Python forms.
Descriptions distinguish helper calls from implementation or runtime success.
DLL loading maps to T1129, not an unsupported DLL-sideloading claim.

The literal-XOR generator computes a key tweak, not decoded payload bytes.
Its unchanged matcher moved from encode/xor to encoding/xor, retaining notable
severity. The broader bytes/bytearray and append/push matchers do not require
an iterator or prove byte scrambling: bytes(x ^ 0xA5) can allocate an XOR-derived
length. Their unchanged matchers and grouping moved from decode/custom to
metadata/lang/source/syntax/call with names describing XOR call arguments.
No supported observation was suppressed. References follow the moves. The
former encode selector's shared transform group and paste-site consumer retain
their literal-generator alternative. The PHP encode consumer and PHP source
syntax exclusion have no scope overlap with the moved rules. Other source-rule
members remain in place. Kyber material-size descriptions now admit public-key
as well as ciphertext material; the meaningful OR group is notable.

 e888318205fc43488ccd72e04cdd4c4d69fae881b1aba87d6538825bc6769d3a
Blihan HTTP task loader / recovered PE image: MALICIOUS

Rizin instruction tracing, direct byte checks and file/VA mapping establish:
- Entry 401000 reads its own file, writes a copy to Windows\microsofthelp.exe,
  invokes 401a70 and launches that copy through 401e00/CreateProcessA.
- 401a70 opens HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, queries a
  value and, if absent, writes the passed executable path with RegSetValueExA.
- 401270 and thread 401930 repeatedly retrieve HTTP response buffers via
  4017c0 (InternetOpenA, InternetOpenUrlA, InternetReadFile). They check a size
  threshold and magic 1e240 at response+40. Routine 401490 cycles the first
  64 bytes as an XOR key over record data beginning at +48. 4014d0 walks typed
  records. Type 200 in the polling thread passes a URL to 401610.
- 401610 fetches the response, generates an eight-letter .exe name beside the
  loader, checks MZ, writes that same response through 401fe0/WriteFile,
  closes it through 402010, and launches that path through 401e00.
- 401cc0 copies six adapter-address bytes from GetAdaptersInfo; the MAC formats
  an HTTP query. Other task records drive hidden Internet Explorer visits and
  operator-controlled waits. 401d30 starts IE via ShellExecuteExA, waits, and
  terminates its child. 401510 writes/loads HidePlugin.dll and resolves/calls
  WindowsHookExON. This export name alone proves no keylogging or injection.
- The mutex pomdfghrt and Software\motherFucker installation marker agree with
  the existing Blihan backdoor identity. No ransomware or credential-theft
  path was established. Collector filename tags are not family evidence.

The header's configuration offset at +1c is zero. No operational endpoint can
be recovered from the self-file XOR/configuration path. MPRESS labels survive
on readable code; this recovered image should not be described as necessarily
requiring unpacking. The 61440-byte PE at outer offset 138bb retains identical
loader/task code over offsets 200..2200 and identical family/protocol strings,
but its rebuilt import data is damaged/absent. Other runtime/data regions differ.
Both outer and embedded units contain checked file-launch code. Successful
runtime operation, final downloaded payload identity and deployment context
remain unknown. These limitations do not erase explicit backdoor purpose.

One hostile rule claimed an unsigned WinInet downloader with an embedded PE.
Its six required facts establish API co-occurrence, unsigned status and a
16-byte DOS-header pattern, not a response-to-image chain or even a validated
embedded PE. Its exact matcher, size bounds, exclusions, PE/DLL scope and
confidence are retained under micro-behaviors/communications/http/client/wininet
as unsigned-wininet-embedded-header-api-profile, notable. Ancestor consumers
were audited; overlapping hosts-file and CrystalX exclusion consumers retain
that exact observation. The Python-only staging consumer cannot match it.
An inert container with these imports and DOS-header bytes matches the neutral
profile without hostile findings. This is a claim/severity/placement correction,
not removal of a downloader technique. Concrete tasking and file-launch rules
remain hostile; Blihan identity and suspicious path-corpus evidence remain.

Checks and remaining limitations

atomscan --no-update --mode slow -f json and cleave facts were run for each
original. Re-scans include the embedded PE unit. No fetched dependency is
implicated. Public sandbox/VT pages were inaccessible; supplied reputation
numbers did not determine a verdict. No native executable was launched.

Existing fixtures outside this batch retain every hostile/suspicious finding:
triage-renpy-loader/launcher.py, first-review/loader-xor-near-exec.py,
hostile/compressed-source-evaluation.py, and the WinInet/CNG DLL fixture.
The benign zstd PE retains no hostile/suspicious finding. Focused controls
exercise direct crypto calls versus declarations/quoted calls, a benign XOR
tweak versus executable decoded source, a plain arithmetic near miss, and
public-key slicing. check.py verifies saved scan results. Actual malware code
and existing attack fixtures, not just a synthetic near miss, support retention.

Final numeric comparison and semantic finding mappings are in comparison.json.
Current default ensemble verdicts agree on the two BENIGN sources and the
MALICIOUS outer PE. The embedded PE remains an ensemble false negative despite
two hostile code/identity findings (probability 0.323015). Its unavailable imports
explain several missing API-based observations, not the false-negative verdict.
The only removed hostile claim is the unsupported WinInet/header co-occurrence
inference, retained as notable. No concrete attack detection was lost.
